newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SUPPORT FOR EU MEMBERSHIP FALLING - POLL.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SUPPORT FOR EU MEMBERSHIP FALLING - POLL.

text.p: Slovak support for European Union (EU) membership has fallen in recent months but a majority still favour joining, according to an opinion poll released this week.

The poll taken by the Focus public opinion research institute between January 28 and February 4, showed that 55.5 percent of respondents supported Slovak membership of the EU, compared with 58.5 percent last September.
The number of Slovaks against EU membership firmed to 11.8 percent, compared to 10.3 percent.
Support for Slovak EU membership reached its highest so far in June 1995, when 58.8 percent of respondents said they favoured joining with only eight percent against.
Slovakia, which applied for EU membership in June 1995, was seen as among the most likely new members of both the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
But some analysts say Slovakia's chances of being in the first wave have waned after criticism by the United States and the EU over the pace of democratic reform.
The poll also showed that the number of Slovaks who would vote in referendum on the EU membership has fallen to 16.7 percent, compared to 19.7 percent last September.
Supporters of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's coalition, which includes junior partners from the far right and left, are the least keen on EU membership, the poll showed.
Supporters of opposition Hungarian minority parties and the Democratic Party showed strongest support -- with 88 and 87 percent respectively.
